projectId.description: Project UUID — defaults to the server-configured project when omitted (`project_id` is accepted too.)

run_store_review.title: Run the store review
run_store_review.description: Run the store review for one project now: listing text in the repo against what is live on the App Store and Google Play, listing claims against the code, privacy labels against data-collecting SDKs, screenshots, length limits and the pre-submission checklist. Each result is ok | finding | unknown (not checked, never healthy). This is a check against the code, not legal advice. At most one review per project every 30 minutes (429 RATE_LIMITED otherwise). Optional projectId. Returns { projectId, checkedAt, status, results, checklist, findings, note }; read it again later with get_store_status. Write: it records a gate run; nothing is submitted to a store.

projectId.description: Project UUID — defaults to the server-configured project when omitted (`project_id` is accepted too.)

save_register_account.title: Save a register account
save_register_account.description: Record an account in the accounts register, or change one when id is given. provider is one of apple, google_play, aws, supabase, vercel, registrar, stripe, github, cloudflare, other; displayName is required on create. Optional ownerEmail, twoFactorDeclared, recoveryContact (a person, not a code), adminCount (1–100) and autoRenew; null clears a field. A value shaped like a key or token is refused (400 SECRET_DETECTED); the register keeps names and contacts only. A second account with the same provider and name is 409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS. Team owners and admins only; needs an account-level key. Returns { id }. Write.

organizationId.description: Organization UUID — defaults to the key owner's only organization

id.description: Account id to change (get_accounts_register); omit to record a new account

provider.description: Required when recording a new account

displayName.description: Required when recording a new account

recoveryContact.description: A person who can recover the account (never a recovery code)

search_codebase.title: Semantic codebase search
search_codebase.description: Search the indexed repo by plain-English meaning via embeddings. Returns { results: [{ file_path, line_start, line_end, content_preview, similarity, … }], query, mode } ordered by similarity. Requires codebase indexing enabled. Read-only. Use to locate where something lives ("where do we verify webhooks?"); use ask_codebase for a synthesized answer with citations, or analyze_codebase_impact to find dependents of a file.

projectId.description: Project UUID (defaults to configured project) (`project_id` is accepted too.)

query.description: Plain-English search query against indexed source files

scopePrefix.description: Optional repo subdirectory prefix to limit search scope (`scope_prefix` is accepted too.)

mode.description: semantic (default): embedding similarity. name: substring match on file path and symbol name.

results.description: Ranked file/symbol hits with paths, line ranges, and similarity

query.description: Normalized query string that was searched

mode.description: Which search ran: semantic or name

search_mushi_docs.title: Search Mushi documentation
search_mushi_docs.description: Search the official Mushi documentation (guides, MCP setup, inventory, QA, skills) by keyword — titles, section headings and summaries are indexed. Returns ranked { results: [{ title, url, excerpt, score }] }. Read-only; works without an API key. Use before guessing API shapes, tool names, or RPC names, then get_mushi_doc to read a page; use run_nl_query for questions about your own project data, not the docs.

query.description: Keywords to search official Mushi docs (guides, MCP, inventory, QA).

search_reports.title: Search reports
search_reports.description: Search reports by meaning and keyword (pgvector similarity server-side; falls back to summary/description substring if embeddings are unavailable). Returns ranked { results: [{ id, summary, similarity }] }. Read-only. Use to find reports by free text ("checkout flakiness"); use get_similar_bugs to dedupe a known component/bug, or get_recent_reports to list without a query.

query.description: Natural-language search text or component path

set_design_settings.title: Set design score actions
set_design_settings.description: Change what the design deviance score may do for one project: threshold (0–100), failCi (true fails `mushi recipe check --push` above the threshold) and autofix. Send at least one. An API key can turn autofix off but never on: turning it on lets the project spend on fixes by itself, so it needs a signed-in owner or admin in the console (403 otherwise). Project owners and admins only. Optional projectId. Returns the saved settings. Write.

projectId.description: Project UUID — defaults to the server-configured project when omitted (`project_id` is accepted too.)

threshold.description: 0–100; the actions fire when the score is above it

failCi.description: true: `mushi recipe check --push` fails CI above the threshold

autofix.description: false turns the design auto-fix off; an API key cannot turn it on

set_domain_auto_renew.title: Declare domain auto-renew
set_domain_auto_renew.description: Declare whether one domain renews automatically at its registrar: autoRenew true, false, or null for not known. The domain id comes from get_accounts_register; only a domain one of the caller's apps uses can be changed (404 otherwise). It records what you declare and checks nothing at the registrar; false opens the registrar_autorenew_off rule. Team owners and admins only; needs an account-level key. Returns { id }. Write.

organizationId.description: Organization UUID — defaults to the key owner's only organization

domainId.description: Domain id (the id of a domain in get_accounts_register)

autoRenew.description: true, false, or null for not known

set_store_review_intake.title: Set store review intake
set_store_review_intake.description: Turn store reviews as reports on or off for one project and set the star threshold (maxRating 1–5: reviews at or under it are filed). enabled is required. An API key can turn intake off or change the threshold while it is on, but only a signed-in owner or admin can turn it on in the console (403 HUMAN_REQUIRED), because it decides that public reviews become reports. Project owners and admins only. Optional projectId. Returns the saved settings. Write.

projectId.description: Project UUID — defaults to the server-configured project when omitted (`project_id` is accepted too.)

enabled.description: false turns intake off; true keeps it on (only the console can turn it on)

maxRating.description: Reviews at or under this many stars are filed (1–5)

set_tier.title: Override contributor tier
set_tier.description: Override a contributor's tier by tier slug (e.g. "champion"), bypassing the normal points-threshold logic entirely. This is an admin escape hatch for manual promotions — normal tier transitions happen automatically via point thresholds instead. Destructive: it is a label-only override that does NOT replay the automatic tier-evaluation path, so any host_credit_payload grant (Stripe perk, badge, etc.) normally tied to reaching that tier via points will NOT fire — confirm with the user whether they also need the perk granted another way. The override persists until another set_tier call changes it; the prior override stays in the end_user_activity audit trail either way, logged as tier_override_manual. Requires mcp:write scope.

externalUserId.description: The host-app user id as passed to Mushi.identify() (`external_user_id` is accepted too.)

tierSlug.description: Tier slug to assign, e.g. "champion", "contributor", "explorer" (`tier_slug` is accepted too.)

start_skill_pipeline.title: Start a skill pipeline
start_skill_pipeline.description: Start a new skill pipeline run for a report. Pass rootSkillSlug and optionally reportId. Returns run_id, context_packet (full instructions + report context), and step list. Read the context_packet — it contains skill instructions plus full report context (repro steps, root cause, RAG files). After executing each step, call checkin_pipeline_step. The PM watching the console sees progress live.

rootSkillSlug.description: Root skill slug to run, e.g. "workflow-fix-and-ship" (`root_skill_slug` is accepted too.)

reportId.description: Report UUID to attach the pipeline to (`report_id` is accepted too.)

mode.description: handoff (default): get context packet for local agent. cloud: auto-dispatch via Cursor Cloud.

projectId.description: Project UUID. Falls back to the configured project. (`project_id` is accepted too.)

submit_fix_result.title: Record a fix outcome
submit_fix_result.description: Record a fix outcome from an external agent (e.g. your own Cursor/Claude run): branch, PR URL, files changed, lines added/removed. Creates a fix_attempt row then patches it to completed and links it to the report. Returns { fixAttemptId }. Write; NOT idempotent — each call creates a new fix_attempt, so call once per PR. Use after you opened a PR outside Mushi; use dispatch_fix to have Mushi open the PR instead, or merge_fix once CI is green.

reportId.description: Report UUID to attach this external fix attempt to (`report_id` is accepted too.)

branch.description: Git branch name where the fix was implemented

prUrl.description: GitHub pull request URL, if a PR was opened (`pr_url` is accepted too.)

filesChanged.description: Repo-relative paths modified by the fix

linesChanged.description: Total lines added + removed across filesChanged

summary.description: One-line human summary of what the fix changed

idempotencyKey.description: Optional UUID — resend the same key to safely retry without creating duplicate fix rows. Omit it and a stable key is derived from reportId + branch + prUrl, so a retried submission carries the identical key instead of a fresh random one.

ok.description: True when the fix_attempt row was created and marked completed

fixId.description: UUID of the new fix_attempt row

suggest_fix.title: Suggested fix (from triage)
suggest_fix.description: Return the Stage-2 suggested-fix slice for one report: root cause, suggested fix, repro steps, summary, and component — faster than get_report_detail when you only need the human-readable hint. Returns { reportId, rootCause, suggestedFix, reproductionSteps, summary, component }. Read-only; reads the existing classification (run triage_issue first if unclassified). Use for a quick "what should we try?"; use get_fix_context for the full paste-ready bundle.

reportId.description: Report UUID to read the Stage-2 suggested-fix slice for (`report_id` is accepted too.)
The report this slice was read from

rootCause.description: Stage-2 root-cause hint, or null if not yet classified

suggestedFix.description: Stage-2 suggested fix, or null if not yet classified

reproductionSteps.description: Reproduction steps recorded on the report (array; [] if none)

component.description: Component/page the bug was attributed to, or null

note.description: Present when no Stage-2 analysis exists — explains why and what to call instead

test_byok_key.title: Test an API key
test_byok_key.description: Re-test one pooled BYOK credential by key id. A successful provider probe activates the key; auth, quota, and network failures keep it out of the runtime pool. Returns the sanitized validation result and updated key metadata. Write; idempotent.

projectId.description: Project id (`project_id` is accepted too.)

test_gen_from_report.title: Generate Playwright test from report
test_gen_from_report.description: Generate a Playwright regression test from a classified report using your project LLM key, then open a draft GitHub PR with the spec. Requires the inventory_v2 plan plus GitHub and LLM keys configured. Returns { qaStoryId, prUrl }. Write; consumes LLM budget; NOT idempotent — each call opens a new PR. Use to lock in a regression as an E2E test; use generate_tdd_from_story to build a test from a mapped user story instead.

reportId.description: Report UUID to turn into a Playwright PR (`report_id` is accepted too.)

projectId.description: Project UUID — defaults to configured project (`project_id` is accepted too.)

test_notification_channel.title: Send a test notification
test_notification_channel.description: Send a test notification to a configured notification channel for the project. Supported channel kinds: "slack" (posts a test Block Kit message to the configured channel), "discord" (posts to the project discord_webhook_url). Returns ok=true if the message was accepted. Use this to verify the integration is working after setup or after changing credentials.

transition_status.title: Move report between states
transition_status.description: Move a report to a new workflow state, enforcing the same transition rules as the admin UI. Valid targets: classified, grouped, fixing, fixed, verified, reopened, dismissed. When dismissing, closedReason (duplicate, not_reproducible, wont_fix, working_as_intended, spam) sets what the reporter is told — spam closes silently, and duplicate needs the report grouped under another one first; reporterMessage posts your note to the reporter verbatim. Returns { ok }. Write; idempotent (setting the current status is a no-op); rejects illegal transitions. Use to dismiss a duplicate or mark fixed; use merge_fix to mark fixed via a merged PR, or reopen_report for the reopened path.

status.description: Target status (resolved is stored as fixed)

closedReason.description: When dismissing: what the reporter is told (spam closes silently)

reporterMessage.description: Optional note posted to the reporter verbatim

triage_issue.title: Triage issue end-to-end
triage_issue.description: Read-only combined tool: merges report detail, the reporter thread, similar bugs (matched on the report summary), the fix context (paste-ready fix prompt, repro steps, root cause), the blast radius of the inventory action the report is filed against, and recent pipeline warnings into a single structured review packet. Returns the packet plus prioritised recommended_actions, partial_errors for any source that failed, and notes for any source that does not apply (e.g. no blast radius when the report is not anchored to an inventory action). Equivalent to a Sentry "Analyze with Seer" flow grounded in user-felt reports. Pass reportId to kick off review. Call this before dispatch_fix.

reportId.description: Report UUID to triage. (`report_id` is accepted too.)

projectId.description: Project UUID. Defaults to configured project. (`project_id` is accepted too.)

includeLogs.description: Include recent pipeline logs in triage packet (default: true). (`include_logs` is accepted too.)

severity.description: critical | high | medium | low, or unknown when the report could not be read

category.description: bug | slow | visual | confusing | other, or unknown

notes.description: Sources that do not apply to this report, and why

summary.description: One-line summary written by the classifier

status.description: Workflow status, e.g. new, classified, fixing, fixed, verified, reopened

component.description: Component or page the bug was attributed to

console_logs.description: Console entries captured with the report

network_logs.description: Network requests captured with the report

inventory_action.description: Inventory action the report is filed against, when resolved

report.description: The report (documented fields, no reporter identifiers), or the error reading it

reporter_thread.description: The unified report timeline (comments, fixes, QA), or null

similar_bugs.description: Up to five nearest reports by summary, excluding this one; null when not searched

fixPrompt.description: Paste-ready fix prompt composed server-side, or null

triage_next_steps.title: What should I work on now?
triage_next_steps.description: Prioritised "do this next" list for the project: blocked auto-fixes first (with the unblock action), then reporters waiting for an answer (they replied in the in-app thread since you last looked), then in-flight fixes to shepherd to merge, then user-felt classified reports by severity, with robot/cron chores (dependency bumps) last. Returns { steps: [{ priority, action, reason, tool, args }], summary }. Read-only. Call this first when the user asks "what needs my attention / what should I triage or fix".

annotations.title: What should I work on now?

projectId.description: Project UUID (defaults to the configured project). (`project_id` is accepted too.)

trigger_judge.title: Run Sonnet-as-Judge
trigger_judge.description: Queue the Sonnet-as-Judge to grade recent fix quality across accessible projects. Returns { dispatched: number } — one judge-batch job per project; scores land asynchronously in judge_results (read back with run_nl_query). Write; consumes LLM budget. Idempotent within a short window. Use before shipping to vet fix quality; use get_fix_timeline to inspect a single attempt instead.

limit.description: Max reports to judge in this batch (default 25, max 100)

projectId.description: Restrict to one project when the API key owns multiple (`project_id` is accepted too.)

dispatched.description: Number of judge-batch jobs dispatched (one per accessible project)

use_mushi.title: Mushi — where to start
use_mushi.description: CALL THIS FIRST if you are new to this Mushi project or unsure which tool to use. Pass your intent as a short natural-language phrase ("fix the top bug", "check what I should work on", "run QA tests", "set up Mushi", …). Returns: (1) a curated list of the 5–12 tool names most relevant to that intent, (2) a one-paragraph orientation to the Mushi project and dashboard state, and (3) the single recommended first tool to call. Only tools this connection exposes are recommended; relevant tools hidden by the active feature groups are named with how to enable them. Avoids loading the full tool catalog into context when only a small subset is needed. Read-only; does not call any downstream tools itself.

intent.description: What you are trying to accomplish with Mushi, e.g. "fix the top bug", "check project health", "run QA tests", "set up Mushi". Leave blank for a general orientation.

resources.name: project_dashboard
resources.title: Loop dashboard snapshot
resources.description: Loop health snapshot — stage counts, bottleneck, recent activity (same payload the admin console polls).

resources.name: project_stats
resources.title: Project stats
resources.description: Report counts, category breakdown, severity distribution.

resources.name: project_settings
resources.title: Project settings
resources.description: Project configuration — autofix agent, plugins enabled, ontology, LLM budgets.

resources.name: privacy_status
resources.title: Privacy posture
resources.description: Returns the privacy posture for this project: storage region, LLM provider, whether your own LLM key is configured, data retention window, and last audit timestamp. Agents should read this before dispatching a fix to confirm that client data stays within the expected boundary. Reads as project data does not leave the project's own LLM account when byok_configured=true.

resources.name: evolution_history
resources.title: Evolution history
resources.description: Returns the project's last 30 days of judge scores, prompt promotions, fixed-bug count, and lesson inductions. Agents can read this to see whether the loop is converging (rising judge scores, falling recurrence) or stalling (flat scores, same bugs re-appearing). Use before review to understand which bug classes the loop has already learned to handle, and which still need human attention.

resources.name: activation_status
resources.title: Activation cockpit status
resources.description: Unified setup posture — SDK heartbeat, reports, GitHub, MCP readiness, QA stories, and the next best action. Agents should read this before guessing which onboarding step is blocking the user.

resources.name: project_integration_health
resources.title: Integration health
resources.description: Live health status of every configured integration channel (Sentry, GitHub, LangFuse, PagerDuty, …). Check this before dispatching a fix to fail-fast on broken channels rather than burning LLM budget and discovering the failure mid-run.

resources.name: inventory_current
resources.title: Current inventory snapshot
resources.description: Current inventory snapshot for the active project — all Action nodes with their spec contract (expected_outcome), build-gate status, linked reports, and fix attempts. Subscribe to this resource to receive notifications/resources/updated when the inventory is re-crawled. Orchestrators can use this to enumerate work items and pick the next Action to fix.
